newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker but spreads narrow further.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker but spreads narrow further.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Monday, hurt by modest profit-taking, but outperformed their U.S. counterparts, with long-term Canada-U.S. spreads falling to 11-year lows, analysts said.

"In Canada we are doing much better than U.S., so the spread continues to improve. But with the U.S. market down we can't escape the force," said David Yu, a fixed-income portfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.05 to C$106.65 to yield 7.422 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark fell 14/32 to yield 6.79 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 63 basis points from 67 basis points at Friday's close.

The spread between Canadian and U.S. benchmark bonds at the 30-year portion of the curve is now the lowest it has been since 1985. Analysts said the spread narrowing is the result of Canada's positive bond market fundamentals, such as low inflation and improving fiscal situation. Dealers said spreads are expected to narrow even further.
Otherwise, Canadian bonds took their direction largely from the United States, where investors took profits after a sharp rally on Friday, traders said.

In new issue news, the Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce today said it is filing a prospectus for a C$250 million debenture issue due October 23, 2011 in the Canadian markets. The bank said the debentures will pay interest twice a year at an annual rate of 7.0 percent until October 23, 2006.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.28 to C$101.61 to yield 6.776 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark fell 8/32 to yield 6.53 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds was 25 basis points, unchanged from Friday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.47 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.06 percent.
